vclz.description: Counts the leading zero bits in each 8-, 16- or 32-bit lane of a D or Q register. Compilers emit it when vectorizing loops that call __builtin_clz, and fixed-point code uses it for normalization.

vcmla.description: Treats adjacent pairs of float lanes (f16 or f32) as complex numbers and adds to the destination the product of Dn and Dm (or one complex element of Dm) rotated by 0, 90, 180 or 270 degrees. Two of them with rotations 0 and 90 make a full complex multiply-add; Armv8.3, unconditional.

vcmp.description: Compares two scalar floats (f16, f32 or f64), or one against #0.0, and writes the result to the FPSCR flags; a following vmrs APSR_nzcv, fpscr copies them to the core flags for a conditional branch. Quiet NaNs give an unordered result (C and V set) without raising Invalid Operation; compilers use it for == and !=.

vcmpe.description: Compares two scalar floats, or one against #0.0, like VCMP and writes the FPSCR flags, but raises Invalid Operation for any NaN operand, quiet ones included. Compilers use it for the ordered relations <, <=, > and >=, followed by vmrs APSR_nzcv, fpscr.
vcmpe.operation: FPSCR.NZCV = compare(Sd, Sm), signal on NaN

vcnt.summary: Vector count set bits per byte
vcnt.description: Counts the 1 bits in each byte of a D or Q register. Compilers use it for __builtin_popcount on NEON, then add the byte counts together with VPADDL; it is also the core of vectorized bit-counting loops.

vcvt.description: Converts between formats: double and single precision, half and single precision (vector), floats and 32-bit integers, floats and fixed-point with #fbits fraction bits, and f32 to BFloat16. Float-to-integer rounds toward zero, which is a C cast like (int)x; integer-to-float uses the FPSCR rounding mode.

forms.heading: VCVT (from single-precision to BFloat16, Advanced SIMD)
VCVT (between half-precision and single-precision, Advanced SIMD)
VCVT (between floating-point and integer, Advanced SIMD)
VCVT (between floating-point and fixed-point, Advanced SIMD)

vcvta.summary: Convert float to integer, round to nearest, ties away
vcvta.description: Converts a scalar float to a signed or unsigned 32-bit integer in an S register, or each float lane of a vector to integers, rounding to nearest with ties away from zero, as lround()/round() do. Added in Armv8; always unconditional.

vcvtb.description: Converts between half precision held in the bottom 16 bits of an S register and single or double precision, leaving the top half of a half-precision destination unchanged; a form also turns f32 into BFloat16. Compilers use it for __fp16 and _Float16 conversions.

vcvtm.summary: Convert float to integer, round toward minus infinity
vcvtm.description: Converts a scalar float or each float lane of a vector to a signed or unsigned 32-bit integer, rounding toward minus infinity. Armv8 compilers use it for (int)floor(x) in one step; always unconditional.

vcvtn.summary: Convert float to integer, round to nearest even
vcvtn.description: Converts a scalar float or each float lane of a vector to a signed or unsigned 32-bit integer, rounding to nearest with ties to even, regardless of the FPSCR mode. Armv8 only; always unconditional.

vcvtp.summary: Convert float to integer, round toward plus infinity
vcvtp.description: Converts a scalar float or each float lane of a vector to a signed or unsigned 32-bit integer, rounding toward plus infinity. Armv8 compilers use it for (int)ceil(x) in one step; always unconditional.

vcvtr.summary: Convert float to integer, using the FPSCR rounding mode
vcvtr.description: Converts a scalar f16, f32 or f64 to a signed or unsigned 32-bit integer in an S register, rounding by the current FPSCR mode (normally to nearest even) instead of toward zero as plain VCVT does. It matches lrint()-style conversion.

vcvtt.description: Converts between half precision held in the top 16 bits of an S register and single or double precision, leaving the bottom half of a half-precision destination unchanged; a form also turns f32 into BFloat16 in the top half. Paired with VCVTB to pack or unpack two half floats per register.

vdiv.description: Divides one scalar float by another (f16, f32 or f64) with IEEE rounding. Compilers emit it for float and double division; Advanced SIMD has no vector divide, so vectorized code uses VRECPE with Newton steps instead.

vdot.description: Splits the lanes of two vectors into pairs of BFloat16 values, multiplies each pair element-wise, sums the two products and adds the sum into the matching single-precision lane of the destination; a by-element form reuses one pair of Dm. Armv8.6 BF16 for machine learning; integer dot products are VSDOT and VUDOT.

vdup.description: Copies a core register (low 8, 16 or 32 bits) or one lane of a D register into every lane of a D or Q register. Compilers use it to broadcast a scalar before a vectorized loop, for example to multiply or compare every element with the same value.

veor.description: XORs two D or Q registers bit by bit; the element type suffix is ignored. NEON code uses it to flip bits, combine masks, in checksums and ciphers, and veor q0, q0, q0 to zero a register.

vext.description: Joins Dn (low) and Dm (high) and takes a register-sized window starting at byte imm of Dn, so the result is Dn shifted down with Dm's lowest bytes filling in. NEON code uses it for sliding windows in filters and to rotate a vector; with larger element sizes the offset counts elements.

vfma.description: Multiplies two floats and adds the product to the destination with a single rounding, as a scalar (f16, f32, f64) or across the float lanes of a D or Q register. Compilers emit it for fma() and for a * b + c when contraction is allowed, on VFPv4 and later CPUs.

vfmab.description: Takes the even-numbered (bottom) BFloat16 elements of Qn and Qm, or one element of Dm, widens them to single precision, multiplies and adds each product into the f32 lanes of Qd with a single rounding. Armv8.6 BF16, used in machine-learning kernels together with VFMAT.

vfmal.description: Multiplies the half-precision values of two S registers (or D registers for the Q form), or each by one scalar, widens the products to single precision and adds them into the f32 lanes of the destination without intermediate rounding. Part of the Armv8.2 FP16 multiply-long extension.

vfmat.description: Takes the odd-numbered (top) BFloat16 elements of Qn and Qm, or one element of Dm, widens them to single precision, multiplies and adds each product into the f32 lanes of Qd with a single rounding. The counterpart of VFMAB; Armv8.6 BF16.

vfms.description: Multiplies two floats and subtracts the product from the destination with a single rounding, as a scalar (f16, f32, f64) or across the float lanes of a D or Q register. Compilers emit it for c - a * b when contraction is allowed, and for fma(-a, b, c).

vfmsl.description: Multiplies the half-precision values of two S registers (or D registers for the Q form), or each by one scalar, widens the products to single precision and subtracts them from the f32 lanes of the destination without intermediate rounding. Armv8.2 FP16 multiply-long extension.

vfnma.description: Multiplies two scalar floats (f16, f32 or f64), adds the destination and negates the whole result, with a single rounding. Compilers emit it for -(a * b) - c, that is fma(-a, b, -c), when contraction is allowed.

vfnms.description: Multiplies two scalar floats (f16, f32 or f64) and subtracts the destination from the product, with a single rounding. Compilers emit it for a * b - c, that is fma(a, b, -c), when contraction is allowed.

vhadd.description: Adds the signed or unsigned 8-, 16- or 32-bit lanes of two D or Q registers and halves each sum, rounding down, without losing the carry. Compilers emit it for vectorized (a + b) >> 1, such as averaging pixels.

vhsub.description: Subtracts the signed or unsigned 8-, 16- or 32-bit lanes of Dm from those of Dn and halves each difference, rounding down, without losing the borrow. Compilers emit it for vectorized (a - b) >> 1.

vins.description: Copies the low 16 bits of Sm into the top 16 bits of Sd and keeps the bottom 16 bits of Sd. Armv8.2 FP16 code uses it to pack two half-precision results into one S register; always unconditional.

vjcvt.description: Converts a double in a D register to a signed 32-bit integer in an S register the way JavaScript's ToInt32 does: truncate toward zero and wrap modulo 2^32. Z in FPSCR tells whether the conversion was exact. Seen in JS engines (Armv8.3).

vld1.description: Loads one to four D registers from consecutive memory without de-interleaving, or one element into a single lane, or one element replicated to all lanes. The address may carry an alignment hint, and Rn can be updated by the transfer size (!) or by Rm. The plain vector load of NEON code.
vld1.operation: Dd.. = [Rn] (1-4 regs, lane or all lanes)

vld2.description: Loads interleaved pairs from memory and splits them across two (or, spaced, four) D registers, e.g. real parts in one and imaginary parts in the other. Also loads one pair into a lane or replicates it to all lanes; supports writeback.

vld3.description: Loads interleaved triples from memory and spreads them over three D registers, the classic way to split packed RGB pixels into colour planes. One-lane and all-lanes forms load a single triple; Rn may be updated afterwards.

vld4.description: Loads interleaved groups of four from memory and spreads them over four D registers, e.g. RGBA pixels into separate R, G, B and A planes. One-lane and all-lanes forms load a single group; writeback is supported.

vldm.description: Loads a run of consecutive S or D registers from memory starting at Rn, going upward; with ! Rn is advanced past the block. Compilers use it to reload saved d8–d15 or to copy blocks; with sp! it is printed as VPOP.

vldmdb.summary: Load multiple FP registers, decrement before
vldmdb.description: Loads consecutive S or D registers from the block just below Rn and always writes the lowered address back to Rn. Rare in compiled code; it walks a descending buffer backwards.

vldmia.summary: Load multiple FP registers, increment after
vldmia.description: The explicit spelling of VLDM: loads consecutive S or D registers upward from Rn, optionally writing back the address past the block. Compilers use it to restore callee-saved d8–d15 and for block copies.

vldr.description: Loads one S, D or (with .16) half-precision register from [Rn ± imm], where imm is a multiple of 4 up to 1020, or from a PC-relative literal. Compilers use it for float and double constants in the literal pool and for reloading spilled FP values.

vmax.description: Picks the larger of each pair of elements of two D or Q vectors: signed or unsigned 8/16/32-bit integers, or floats (a NaN input gives NaN). Common in clamping and image code.

vmaxnm.description: Returns the larger of two floats, preferring a number over a quiet NaN like C fmax(). Works on S/D registers or per lane on D/Q vectors; Armv8 only, and never conditional.

vmin.description: Picks the smaller of each pair of elements of two D or Q vectors: signed or unsigned 8/16/32-bit integers, or floats (a NaN input gives NaN). Used for clamping and saturating by hand.

vminnm.description: Returns the smaller of two floats, preferring a number over a quiet NaN like C fmin(). Works on S/D registers or per lane on D/Q vectors; Armv8 only, and never conditional.

vmla.description: Multiplies two operands and adds the product to the destination. The float form rounds twice (it is not fused like VFMA) and exists for scalar S/D registers and vectors; integer and by-scalar vector forms are used in filters and dot-product loops.

vmlal.description: Multiplies signed or unsigned elements of two D vectors (or by one scalar element) into double-width products and adds them to the Q destination. Typical of 16-bit audio and image filters that accumulate in 32 bits.

vmls.description: Multiplies two operands and subtracts the product from the destination. The float form is not fused (two roundings) and covers scalar S/D registers and vectors; integer and by-scalar vector forms exist too.

vmlsl.description: Multiplies signed or unsigned elements of two D vectors (or by a scalar element) into double-width products and subtracts them from the Q destination.

vmmla.description: Treats the Q sources as a 2x4 and a 4x2 matrix of bfloat16 values, multiplies them and adds the 2x2 product into single-precision lanes of Qd. Used by machine-learning kernels on Armv8.6 cores.
vmmla.operation: Qd(2x2 f32) += Qn(2x4 bf16) * Qm(4x2 bf16)

vmov.description: Copies between FP/SIMD registers, loads an immediate, or moves raw bits between core and FP registers: one S, a pair of S, a D from r0/r1, or one vector lane. Android's softfp ABI passes doubles in core registers, so vmov d0, r0, r1 is everywhere.

forms.heading: VMOV (between two general-purpose registers and a doubleword floating-point register)
VMOV (between two general-purpose registers and two single-precision registers)

vmovl.description: Sign- or zero-extends every element of a D vector to double width in a Q register, e.g. bytes to halfwords. The usual first step before arithmetic that would overflow the narrow type.

vmovn.description: Keeps the low half of each element of a Q vector and writes the narrowed elements to a D register, with no saturation. Used to pack wide intermediate results back into bytes or halfwords.

vmovx.description: Copies the upper 16 bits of Sm (a second half-precision value) into the low half of Sd and clears the rest. Used with FP16 arithmetic to unpack pairs of halves (Armv8.2).

vmrs.description: Reads an FP system register such as FPSCR into a core register. With APSR_nzcv as the target it copies the flags of a preceding VCMP to the APSR, so an ordinary conditional branch can act on a float comparison.

vmsr.description: Writes a core register to an FP system register, usually FPSCR, to change the rounding mode, flush-to-zero or exception bits, or to restore the FP environment (fesetround, fesetenv).

vmul.description: Multiplies floats (scalar S/D registers or vector lanes), integer or polynomial vector elements, or a vector by one scalar element. Compiled float and double code meets the scalar form constantly.

vmull.description: Multiplies signed, unsigned or polynomial elements of two D vectors (or by a scalar) into double-width results in a Q register. The 64-bit polynomial form (vmull.p64) is the carry-less multiply behind fast CRC and GCM.

vmvn.description: Inverts every bit of a D or Q register, or fills each element with the inverse of an immediate. The immediate form is a cheap way to build masks such as 0xFFFFFF00 in every lane.

vneg.description: Flips the sign of a float in an S or D register, or negates each signed integer or float lane of a vector (wrapping, no saturation). Scalar float code uses it for unary minus.

vnmla.description: Computes the negated sum of the destination and the product of two floats, -(Sd + Sn*Sm), with separate roundings for multiply and add. Scalar S/D registers only.

vnmls.description: Multiplies two floats and subtracts the destination from the product, Sn*Sm - Sd, rounding after each step. Scalar S/D registers only; compilers use it for a*b - c when fusing is not allowed.

vnmul.description: Multiplies two floats in S or D registers and negates the product. Compilers fold -(a*b) into it instead of a VMUL followed by a VNEG.

vorn.description: ORs a D or Q register with the inverted bits of another. The immediate form is only an assembler convenience: it becomes VORR with the inverted constant, so a disassembler prints VORR.

vorr.description: ORs two D or Q registers, or ORs an immediate into every 16- or 32-bit element to set chosen bits. With both sources the same register it is a plain register copy, which disassemblers print as VMOV.

vpadal.description: Adds adjacent pairs of signed or unsigned elements of a D or Q vector, widens each sum to double width and adds it to the destination elements. Used for running horizontal sums of bytes, as in checksums and histograms.

vpadd.description: Adds adjacent pairs of elements from the concatenation of two D registers, integer or float, giving one D result. Repeated, it produces a horizontal sum of a vector.

vpaddl.description: Adds adjacent pairs of signed or unsigned elements of a D or Q vector and stores each sum at double width. A common step in summing all bytes of a vector without overflow.

vpmax.description: Takes the larger of each adjacent pair of elements across two concatenated D registers, integer or float. Repeating it finds the maximum of a whole vector.

vpmin.description: Takes the smaller of each adjacent pair of elements across two concatenated D registers, integer or float. Repeating it finds the minimum of a whole vector.

vpop.summary: Pop FP registers from the stack
vpop.description: Loads a list of consecutive S or D registers from the stack and moves sp past them; another name for VLDMIA sp!. Function epilogues use it to restore callee-saved d8–d15.

vpush.summary: Push FP registers to the stack
vpush.description: Moves sp down and stores a list of consecutive S or D registers there; another name for VSTMDB sp!. Function prologues use it to save callee-saved d8–d15.

vqabs.description: Takes the absolute value of each signed element of a D or Q vector, clamping the most negative value to the maximum instead of leaving it negative. Saturation sets the sticky QC bit in FPSCR.

vqadd.description: Adds elements of two D or Q vectors, signed or unsigned, clamping at the type limits instead of wrapping. Common in audio mixing and pixel arithmetic; saturation sets QC in FPSCR.

vqdmlal.description: Multiplies signed 16- or 32-bit elements of two D vectors (or by a scalar), doubles the product and adds it to the double-width Q destination, saturating both steps. Used in Q15/Q31 fixed-point DSP code.

vqdmlsl.description: Multiplies signed 16- or 32-bit elements of two D vectors (or by a scalar), doubles the product and subtracts it from the double-width Q destination, with saturation. A fixed-point DSP building block.

vqdmulh.description: Multiplies signed 16- or 32-bit elements (or by a scalar element), doubles the product and keeps its upper half, saturating the one overflowing case. The basic Q15/Q31 fixed-point multiply.

vqdmull.description: Multiplies signed 16- or 32-bit elements of two D vectors (or by a scalar), doubles the product and writes the full double-width result to a Q register, saturating on overflow.

vqmovn.description: Narrows each element of a Q vector to half width in a D register, signed to signed or unsigned to unsigned, clamping values that do not fit. Packs wide results back into bytes or halfwords safely.

vqmovun.summary: Saturating move narrow, signed to unsigned
vqmovun.description: Narrows each signed element of a Q vector to an unsigned half-width value in a D register: negatives become zero and large values the maximum. The usual way to turn 16-bit intermediate pixels into clamped bytes.

vqneg.description: Negates each signed element of a D or Q vector, turning the most negative value into the maximum instead of leaving it unchanged. Saturation sets QC in FPSCR.

vqrdmlah.description: Multiplies signed 16- or 32-bit elements (or by a scalar), doubles and rounds the product, keeps the high half and adds it to the destination with saturation. Fixed-point DSP code on Armv8.1 cores.

vqrdmlsh.description: Like VQRDMLAH, but the rounded high half of the doubled product is subtracted from the destination, with saturation. Armv8.1 fixed-point arithmetic.

vqrdmulh.summary: Saturating rounding doubling multiply, high half
vqrdmulh.description: Multiplies signed 16- or 32-bit elements (or by a scalar element), doubles the product, rounds and keeps the high half, saturating on overflow. The rounded Q15/Q31 multiply of fixed-point DSP code.

vqrshl.description: Shifts each signed or unsigned element by a signed amount taken from the matching element of another register: positive shifts left with saturation, negative shifts right with rounding.

vqrshrn.description: Shifts each element of a Q vector right by an immediate with rounding, then narrows it to half width in a D register with saturation, signed to signed or unsigned to unsigned. Scales fixed-point results down.

vqrshrun.summary: Saturating rounding shift right narrow, unsigned
vqrshrun.description: Shifts each signed element of a Q vector right by an immediate with rounding and narrows it to an unsigned half-width value, clamping negatives to zero. Typical for turning filtered pixels back into bytes.

vqshl.description: Shifts signed or unsigned elements left by an immediate, or by signed per-element amounts from a register (negative shifts right), clamping on overflow instead of wrapping.

vqshlu.summary: Saturating shift left, signed to unsigned
vqshlu.description: Shifts signed elements left by an immediate and saturates the result to the unsigned range of the same width, so negatives become zero and overflow gives the maximum.

vqshrn.description: Shifts each element of a Q vector right by an immediate (truncating) and narrows it to half width in a D register with saturation, signed to signed or unsigned to unsigned.

vqshrun.description: Shifts each signed element of a Q vector right by an immediate (truncating) and narrows it to an unsigned half-width value in a D register, clamping negatives to zero.

vqsub.description: Subtracts elements of two D or Q vectors, signed or unsigned, clamping at the type limits instead of wrapping; unsigned results stop at zero. Saturation sets QC in FPSCR.

vraddhn.summary: Add, round and narrow to high half
vraddhn.description: Adds the wide elements of two Q vectors, rounds, and keeps only the upper half of each sum in a D register. Used to average or rescale fixed-point values while narrowing them.

vrecpe.description: Gives a rough estimate of 1/x for each float lane, or of the reciprocal of unsigned 32-bit fixed-point values. Compilers refine it with VRECPS Newton-Raphson steps to divide quickly, since NEON has no vector divide.

vrecps.description: Computes 2 - a*b for each float lane, the correction factor of one Newton-Raphson step that refines a reciprocal estimate from VRECPE. Usually appears right after VRECPE, followed by a VMUL.

vrev16.description: Swaps the two bytes inside every 16-bit chunk of a D or Q vector. Used for byte-order conversion of arrays of 16-bit values.
vrev16.operation: Vd = bswap16 of each halfword of Vm

vrev32.description: Reverses the order of the bytes or halfwords inside every 32-bit chunk of a D or Q vector. With bytes it converts the endianness of 32-bit values, e.g. in hashing code.
vrev32.operation: Vd = reverse elements in each 32-bit chunk of Vm

vrev64.description: Reverses the order of the bytes, halfwords or words inside every 64-bit chunk of a D or Q vector. Used to reverse arrays and to swap the two 32-bit halves of each doubleword.
vrev64.operation: Vd = reverse elements in each 64-bit chunk of Vm

vrhadd.description: Adds signed or unsigned elements of two vectors and halves the sum, rounding up, without intermediate overflow: the rounded average. Common in image scaling and blending.

vrinta.description: Rounds a float to a whole number, halfway cases away from zero, like C round(). Works on S/D registers or per lane on vectors; Armv8 only and never conditional.

vrintm.summary: Round to integral, toward minus infinity
vrintm.description: Rounds a float down to a whole number, like C floor(). Works on S/D registers or per lane on vectors; Armv8 only, so older code calls floor() instead.

vrintn.summary: Round to integral, ties to even
vrintn.description: Rounds a float to the nearest whole number, halfway cases to even, like C roundeven(). Works on S/D registers or per lane on vectors; Armv8 only.

vrintp.summary: Round to integral, toward plus infinity
vrintp.description: Rounds a float up to a whole number, like C ceil(). Works on S/D registers or per lane on vectors; Armv8 only, so code for older cores calls ceil() instead.

vrintr.description: Rounds a float in an S or D register to a whole number using the rounding mode in FPSCR, without raising Inexact, like C nearbyint(). Armv8 only.

vrintx.description: Rounds a float to a whole number in the current rounding mode and raises Inexact when the value changes, like C rint(). The vector form always rounds to nearest even; Armv8 only.

vrintz.description: Truncates a float to a whole number, like C trunc(), keeping it in floating-point format. Works on S/D registers or per lane on vectors; Armv8 only.

vrshl.description: Shifts each signed or unsigned element by a signed per-element amount from another register: positive shifts left, negative shifts right with rounding. Lets one loop scale by a variable power of two.

vrshr.description: Shifts each signed (arithmetic) or unsigned (logical) element right by an immediate, rounding to nearest instead of truncating. A shift of zero is a plain copy and is printed as VORR or VMOV.

vrshrn.description: Shifts each element of a Q vector right by an immediate with rounding and keeps the low half of each result in a D register, without saturation. A shift of zero is printed as VMOVN.

vrsqrte.description: Gives a rough estimate of 1/sqrt(x) for each float lane, or for unsigned 32-bit fixed-point values. Refined with VRSQRTS steps; vector normalisation code uses the pair.

vrsqrts.description: Computes (3 - a*b)/2 for each float lane, the correction factor of a Newton-Raphson step that refines a VRSQRTE estimate of 1/sqrt(x).

vrsra.description: Shifts each signed or unsigned element right by an immediate with rounding and adds the result to the destination element. Used in fixed-point filters.

vrsubhn.summary: Subtract, round and narrow to high half
vrsubhn.description: Subtracts the wide elements of two Q vectors, rounds, and keeps the upper half of each difference in a D register. The rounding counterpart of VSUBHN.

vsdot.description: Multiplies groups of four signed bytes and adds each group's sum into a 32-bit lane of the destination; one source can be a single 32-bit element. Armv8.2 DotProd, heavily used in quantised neural-network code.

vsel.description: Picks one of two floats in S or D registers by a condition on the flags: VSELEQ, VSELGE, VSELGT or VSELVS, with the opposite condition made by swapping operands. Lets Armv8 code avoid a branch or IT block for a ternary.

vshl.description: Shifts every element left by an immediate, filling with zeros, or by signed per-element amounts from a register, where negative amounts shift right (arithmetic for signed types, logical for unsigned).

vshll.description: Sign- or zero-extends each element of a D vector to double width in a Q register and shifts it left by an immediate, up to the element size. Widens and scales in one step.

vshr.description: Shifts each element right by an immediate: arithmetic for signed types, logical for unsigned. A shift of zero is a plain copy and is printed as VORR or VMOV.

vshrn.description: Shifts each element of a Q vector right by an immediate and keeps the low half of each result in a D register, truncating and without saturation. A shift of zero is printed as VMOVN.

vsli.description: Shifts each element left by an immediate and writes it into the destination, keeping the destination bits below the shift amount. Packs bit fields, e.g. assembling RGB565 pixels.

vsmmla.description: Treats the Q sources as a 2x8 and an 8x2 matrix of signed bytes, multiplies them and adds the 2x2 product into the four 32-bit lanes of Qd. Speeds up int8 matrix multiplication (Armv8.6 I8MM).

vsqrt.description: Computes the square root of a float in an S or D register; sqrt() and sqrtf() compile to it directly. There is no vector form: NEON code uses VRSQRTE with refinement instead.

vsra.description: Shifts each element right by an immediate (arithmetic for signed, logical for unsigned) and adds the result to the destination element. Used in fixed-point filters and multi-word arithmetic.

vsri.description: Shifts each element right by an immediate and writes it into the destination, keeping the destination's top bits that the shift vacated. Packs and unpacks bit fields such as RGB565 pixels.

vst1.description: Stores one to four D registers to consecutive memory without interleaving, or a single lane of one register. Takes an optional alignment hint and can update Rn by the transfer size (!) or by Rm. The plain vector store of NEON code.

vst2.description: Stores two (or, spaced, four) D registers interleaved element by element, e.g. re-packing separate real and imaginary parts into complex pairs. Can also store one pair from a lane; supports writeback.

vst3.description: Stores three D registers interleaved element by element, the usual way to write colour planes back as packed RGB pixels. A one-lane form stores a single triple; Rn may be updated afterwards.

vst4.description: Stores four D registers interleaved element by element, e.g. packing R, G, B and A planes into RGBA pixels. A one-lane form stores a single group; writeback is supported.

vstm.description: Stores a run of consecutive S or D registers to memory upward from Rn; with ! Rn is advanced past the block. Used to save FP state and for block copies together with VLDM.

vstmdb.summary: Store multiple FP registers, decrement before
vstmdb.description: Stores consecutive S or D registers into the block just below Rn and writes the lowered address back to Rn. With sp it is the prologue's VPUSH, which disassemblers print under that name.

vstmia.summary: Store multiple FP registers, increment after
vstmia.description: The explicit spelling of VSTM: stores consecutive S or D registers upward from Rn, optionally writing back the address past the block. Seen in FP context saving and memcpy-style block copies.

vstr.description: Stores one S, D or (with .16) half-precision register to [Rn ± imm], where imm is a multiple of 4 up to 1020. Compilers use it to write float and double variables and to spill FP registers to the stack.

vsub.description: Subtracts floats in S/D registers or per vector lane, or integer elements of D/Q vectors (wrapping). Compiled float and double code uses the scalar form constantly.

vsubhn.summary: Subtract and narrow to high half
vsubhn.description: Subtracts the wide elements of two Q vectors and keeps the upper half of each difference, truncated, in a D register. VRSUBHN is the rounding variant.

vsubl.description: Sign- or zero-extends the elements of two D vectors to double width and subtracts them into a Q register, so the difference cannot overflow. Common in pixel-difference code.

vsubw.description: Sign- or zero-extends the elements of a D vector to double width and subtracts them from the matching elements of a Q vector.

vsudot.summary: Dot product, signed by unsigned (by element)
vsudot.description: Multiplies groups of four signed bytes by four unsigned bytes taken from one 32-bit element and adds each group's sum into a 32-bit lane of the destination. Part of Armv8.6 I8MM, for int8 neural-network kernels.

vswp.description: Exchanges the contents of two D or two Q registers in one step, without a temporary register. Appears in hand-written NEON code and in register shuffles.

vtbl.description: Uses each byte of Dm as an index into a table of one to four D registers and writes the selected bytes to Dd; out-of-range indices give zero. Used for arbitrary byte shuffles and small lookup tables.

vtbx.description: Like VTBL, but when an index is out of range the destination byte keeps its old value. Lets several lookups be chained over a table larger than four registers.

vtrn.description: Treats two registers as 2x2 blocks of elements and transposes each block, changing both registers in place. A few of these build a 4x4 matrix transpose; VUZP.32 and VZIP.32 on D registers are the same operation.

vtst.description: Per lane: the result is all ones if the two source elements share at least one set bit, otherwise zero. Builds masks for flag and bit-field tests.

vudot.description: Multiplies groups of four unsigned bytes and adds each group's sum into a 32-bit lane of the destination; one source can be a single 32-bit element. Armv8.2 DotProd, used in quantised neural-network and image code.

vummla.description: Treats the Q sources as a 2x8 and an 8x2 matrix of unsigned bytes, multiplies them and adds the 2x2 product into the four 32-bit lanes of Qd. Speeds up int8 matrix multiplication (Armv8.6 I8MM).

vusdot.description: Multiplies groups of four unsigned bytes by four signed bytes and adds each group's sum into a 32-bit lane of the destination; the signed source can be one 32-bit element. Armv8.6 I8MM, for mixed-sign int8 kernels.

vusmmla.description: Multiplies a 2x8 matrix of unsigned bytes from Qn by an 8x2 matrix of signed bytes from Qm and adds the 2x2 product into the four 32-bit lanes of Qd (Armv8.6 I8MM).

vuzp.description: De-interleaves two registers in place: the even-numbered elements of the pair end up in the first register and the odd-numbered ones in the second. Splits interleaved channels; the .32 form on D registers is printed as VTRN.

vzip.description: Interleaves two registers in place: the first receives alternating elements from the low halves of both, the second from the high halves. Merges separate channels; the .32 form on D registers is printed as VTRN.

wfe.description: Hint that lets the core sleep in a low-power state until an event arrives, such as a SEV from another core or an interrupt. Spinlock wait loops in kernels and runtimes use it.

wfi.description: Hint that puts the core into a low-power state until an interrupt or similar wake-up arrives. Kernel idle loops use it; in user code it is rare and may be trapped or treated as a NOP.

yield.description: Hint telling the CPU that this thread is spinning, so a multithreaded core can give time to other threads. Spin-wait loops (cpu_relax, Rust spin_loop) emit it; elsewhere it acts as a NOP.
